gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the only HDBaseT extenders sold in an approved store come as a matched pair: AV Access sells the 4KEX100 transmitter and receiver only together, says one transmitter works with only one receiver over a direct cable, and says 4K reaches 100 m only on Cat 6a/7 (70 m on Cat 5e/6). A church running the signal from the booth should plan on that kit's own receiver feeding the projector's HDMI port, not on the HDBaseT port built into the Epson L690U or Panasonic PT-VMZ.
standout_why: I compared five rival pages. projectorverdict.com never mentions HDBaseT, Cat6 or cable-run limits; it only talks about a volunteer re-running HDMI. projectorcentral.com (best church projectors, Nov 2026) has no HDBaseT, Cat6 or run-length text apart from 3G-SDI on one $50k model, and lists no screens or mounts. itechguides.com covers part of it: it marks 'HDBaseT listed' for two Epson models and says 'A long run may need an appropriate transport method', but it names no extender, distance, cable grade or pairing rule. aafrc.org (laser) only mentions LAN control from the sound booth. flickerhall.com has no HDBaseT or extender content. No rival lists a working set (projector + signal transport + cable) or prices one.
kit_items: Projector: Epson PowerLite L690U (6,500 lm, WUXGA, laser), one of ChatGPT's picks. Epson.com lists an HDBaseT input and HDMI two-in, one-out. It is $3,515 on epson.com but marked Out of Stock.

Booth-to-projector signal: AV Access 4KEX100-H2 HDBaseT extender kit (transmitter + receiver). It carries 1080p/WUXGA 100 m over Cat 5e/6, and one power adapter at either end powers both units. Plug its receiver into the projector's HDMI input, because AV Access does not say its transmitter works with other brands' built-in HDBaseT receivers.
Cable: one solid Cat 6a run from the booth to the projector, direct with no network switch. AV Access says the unit 'won't work if you connect it to a switch', and 4K at 100 m needs Cat 6a/7.
Cheaper transport option: AV Access 4KEX100-L kit ($227.99), with the same 70 m 4K / 100 m 1080p limits and sold only as a pair.
If you buy the Panasonic: Amazon lists a 'PT-VMZ51S ... No Digital Link' variant next to the PT-VMZ51. Buy the non-S model if you want the built-in HDBaseT (Digital Link) port.
Screen and ceiling mount: needed, but I priced neither (see unsourced).
